text:
Can you write a cover letter for me? I'm 52 and I'm applying for an office manager job at a dental practice in my town. I've been out of work for 7 years caring for my mother, who died last spring.

My background:
- Before that I was office manager at a veterinary clinic for 11 years. It had 4 vets and 14 staff.
- I handled scheduling, billing, and the clinic's move from paper records to software in 2014.
- In my last three years there, unpaid invoices over 90 days went from about $38,000 to $9,000.
- During the 7 years at home I managed my mother's insurance claims and her appointments with 6 specialists.
- I haven't used Dentrix, which the posting lists. I used AVImark at the clinic.
- The practice has 3 dentists. The posting says the manager supervises 9 people.

Keep it under 300 words.

I've left a few brackets for you to fill in. I avoided adding any details you didn't give me.

<final_document>
Dear [Hiring Manager's Name],

I am writing to apply for the Office Manager position at [Practice Name]. For eleven years I was office manager at [Clinic Name], a veterinary clinic with four veterinarians and fourteen staff. I would welcome the chance to bring that experience to your practice.

At the clinic I handled scheduling and billing for a busy, multi-provider office. In 2014 I managed our move from paper records to AVImark practice management software. In my last three years there, I reduced our unpaid invoices over 90 days from about $38,000 to $9,000 by [one short phrase on how, e.g., "following up on every overdue account each week"].

For the past seven years I cared full-time for my mother, who passed away last spring. During that time I managed her insurance claims and coordinated her appointments with six specialists. I also saw healthcare from the patient's side, and I learned how much a well-run office matters to someone who is worried about their health or confused by a bill.

I have not used Dentrix yet. I learned AVImark well enough to move an entire clinic onto it, and I am confident I can learn Dentrix quickly. [Optional: "I have already begun working through Dentrix's training materials."]

Supervising your team of nine, keeping three dentists' schedules running smoothly, and making sure claims are paid on time is work I am ready to take on. Thank you for your consideration. I would be glad to talk with you about how I can help [Practice Name].

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Phone] | [Email]
</final_document>

Some notes:
- **Length:** The letter is about 270 words, or a little more once you fill in the brackets.
- **Age:** I didn't mention it. It doesn't help your case, and employers shouldn't consider it.
- **The 7-year gap:** It's stated once, directly, and then tied to skills that matter for this job. Hiring managers usually respond better to that than to vague wording.
- **Dentrix:** Only include the optional sentence if it's true. Dentrix has free tutorials online, so working through a few before you send this would let you say it honestly.
- **Supervision:** If you supervised staff at the clinic, add it to the second paragraph (for example, "and supervised a front-office team of X"). The posting stresses supervision, so it's worth including if you did it.
